title: Call for Innovative Green Education Action Projects 2026: Share Your Climate Education Project and Win a Fully Funded Visit to Brussels
summary: The Education for Climate Coalition has launched its Call for Innovative Green Education Action Projects 2026 , inviting students, educators, schools, institutions, organisations and other education stakeholders to showcase innovative projects that are helping communities respond to climate change and advance sustainability through education. The initiative comes ahead of Education for Climate Day 2026 , which will take place on 22 October 2026 . The call is designed to identify strong, practical examples of climate and sustainability education that can inspire other education communities across the European Education Area. Three projects from each of the three thematic areas will be selected to present their work during Education for Climate Day 2026. Representatives of selected projects will also receive a fully funded visit to Brussels to participate in the event and interact with other participants working in climate education across the European Education Area. The application deadline is 6 September 2026 . What Is the Education for Climate Coalition 2026 Call About? The Education for Climate Coalition is looking for real examples of green education projects that have already been implemented or are currently being implemented . Rather than focusing solely on ideas or proposals for future projects, the call seeks projects where concrete actions have already taken place. These could include initiatives in schools, universities, communities, civil society organisations, public institutions, cultural settings, professional environments or other formal and informal learning contexts. The selected projects are intended to demonstrate how education can contribute to: Climate action Sustainability Intergenerational cooperation Youth participation Green citizenship Institutional transformation Sustainable development Future-oriented learning Community engagement Green competences Innovative teaching and learning The initiative particularly seeks projects that can provide practical evidence of impact , such as learning materials, activities, educational tools, photographs, videos, documents, implementation records or other tangible outputs. Three Thematic Areas for the 2026 Call Applicants can submit projects under one of three thematic areas. Each theme focuses on a different aspect of green education and climate action. 1. Youth Leadership and Intergenerational Dialogue for Climate Action The first theme focuses on projects that give young people an active role in climate and sustainability action. The emphasis is not simply on teaching young people about climate change. Instead, projects should demonstrate how learners can become active participants in creating solutions and influencing decisions within their schools, institutions and communities. The theme also recognises schools and other educational institutions as potential living environments for sustainability , where green values and sustainable practices can become part of everyday life. Projects may involve collaboration between: Students and young people Teachers and educators Families Schools Local authorities Civil society organisations Community organisations Other local stakeholders The Education for Climate Coalition is particularly interested in initiatives that create meaningful connections between different generations. This reflects the Coalition s 2026 priority of intergenerational fairness . The underlying idea is that young people should not only be prepared to deal with future challenges but should also have opportunities to influence the present and help shape the future. Questions applicants should consider Projects under this theme should be able to demonstrate: How young people actively participate in climate or sustainability action. How learners contribute to designing, leading or influencing activities. How young people participate in decisions connected to the project. How schools work with families and local communities. How different generations collaborate. How the project supports a whole-school or whole-institution approach to sustainability. How the project is connected to local needs. Whether the approach could be adapted or transferred to another community or education setting. A strong application should therefore go beyond simply stating that young people participated. It should explain what they did, what decisions they influenced, what actions they led and what changed as a result . 2. Citizenship Education and Institutional Action for Sustainability The second theme looks at projects that help citizens, learners and communities understand sustainability challenges and take practical action. This category is broader than traditional classroom education. It recognises that learning about sustainability can happen in many environments and can involve a wide range of organisations and professionals. Eligible projects under this theme may be led by: Civil society organisations Companies Public institutions Researchers Cultural organisations and actors Non-formal education providers Educational institutions Other organisations working to advance sustainability education The theme encourages initiatives that connect knowledge and expertise with public engagement and practical action . For example, a project could take research findings or professional knowledge and turn them into accessible educational programmes for communities. Another project could use cultural activities, public engagement or community-based learning to help people understand environmental challenges and participate in the green transition. Questions applicants should consider Applicants should explain: How the project helps citizens, learners or communities understand green and sustainability issues. Who leads the project. Which groups participate in the project. How different target groups are engaged. How research, professional expertise, institutional knowledge or community knowledge is converted into accessible learning. How the project encourages participation. How it promotes responsibility and behavioural change. How the project addresses the needs of different groups. What makes the initiative inclusive and practical. Why the project is relevant beyond the immediate learning environment. The strongest projects will demonstrate that sustainability education can lead to participation, responsibility and action , rather than remaining purely theoretical. 3. GreenComp: Envisioning Sustainable Futures in Teaching and Learning The third thematic area focuses on the GreenComp framework and how sustainability competences can be incorporated into teaching and learning. Particular attention is given to the competence area of envisioning sustainable futures . This theme is aimed at projects that help learners think beyond immediate challenges and explore what different possible futures could look like. Projects may encourage learners to: Imagine alternative futures. Examine the long-term consequences of current decisions. Compare different possible sustainability pathways. Think critically about environmental, social and economic consequences. Develop the competences required to contribute to sustainable development. Translate future-oriented thinking into practical action. Educators, trainers and facilitators also have an important role under this theme because they create the learning environments in which future thinking and sustainability competences can develop. Questions applicants should consider Projects should demonstrate: How GreenComp or sustainability competencies are incorporated into teaching and learning. How learners imagine or explore sustainable futures. How current decisions are connected to future environmental, social and economic consequences. Which practical tools or methods are used to develop future thinking. How learners are given agency to contribute to sustainability. How the approach could be adapted by other educators or learning communities. Applicants should make the connection between learning, future thinking and practical sustainability action clear. Who Can Submit a Project? The call is open to a broad range of participants across formal and informal education. The organisers welcome submissions from Students Educators Schools Education institutions Civil society organisations Companies Public institutions Researchers Cultural actors Non-formal education providers Other education stakeholders Community organisations and partners involved in education and sustainability Projects can be small or large , local or international , and public or private . This broad approach means applicants do not necessarily need to represent a large institution or operate a major international programme. A smaller, locally rooted initiative can also be considered if it demonstrates innovation, participation, tangible implementation and meaningful community impact. Geographic Eligibility One of the key eligibility requirements is that the green education action must be based in and across a European Education Area country . The eligible geographic area includes the 27 European Union Member States , as well as the following: Iceland Liechtenstein North Macedonia Norway Serbia Türkiye Therefore, the call is specifically focused on projects operating within the European Education Area. Projects from outside this geographic area would not meet the stated location eligibility requirement. What Types of Projects Are Eligible? The initiative is looking for projects that have moved beyond the idea stage and have had concrete implementation actions . A project can be Already completed Currently ongoing Started within the eligible period Recently completed within the last five years The important consideration is that actual implementation must have taken place. This means applicants should be prepared to demonstrate what they have done rather than submitting only a proposal for something they intend to do in the future. Previous Applicants Can Apply Again Projects that participated in previous editions of the call are not automatically excluded. They may still be eligible if they have developed: New workstreams New materials New activities New project elements Other significant developments This creates an opportunity for previous participants to showcase how their initiatives have evolved. What Will the Organisers Be Looking For? The Education for Climate Coalition wants to showcase projects that demonstrate education innovation in practice . Applications will be assessed according to several important dimensions. 1. Location The project must be implemented in or across an eligible European Education Area country. 2. Ambition The organisers want projects that are inspiring, courageous and innovative. Applicants should demonstrate what makes their approach different and why it represents an important contribution to climate or sustainability education. 3. Relevance The project should clearly address the theme under which it is submitted. Applicants should avoid vague descriptions and explain exactly how their activities respond to the selected thematic area. 4. Interdisciplinarity Projects are encouraged to demonstrate connections across different disciplines and areas of education for climate innovation. The assessment also considers the number and type of GreenComp competences addressed by the project. 5. Participatory Nature Participation is a particularly important element of the Education for Climate Coalition community. Projects should ideally demonstrate collaboration between at least two education actor categories identified in the application survey. This means applicants should clearly explain who was involved and how different groups contributed to the project. Simply having multiple stakeholders associated with a project may not be enough. The application should show how they actually participated in shaping or implementing the initiative. 6. Education for Climate Innovation Area Coverage The project must cover at least one of the five Education for Climate Innovation Areas . Applicants should therefore identify the relevant innovation area covered by their work and explain how the project addresses it. 7. GreenComp Engagement Projects must address at least one of the twelve GreenComp competences . Applicants should identify the relevant competence or competences and explain how these are reflected in their activities, learning experiences or outcomes. 8. Innovation Learning Engagement The project should incorporate at least one learning or teaching method identified in the June 2022 Council Recommendation on learning for the green transition and sustainable development . Applicants should also explain the learning goals and the didactic or pedagogical approach used. This means the submission should not only describe what participants did but should also demonstrate the educational reasoning behind the approach. 9. Tangibility Evidence is a major consideration. Applicants should provide concrete and codified evidence of their project, which could include: Educational materials Activity descriptions Learning resources Photographs PDFs Videos Documents Other project outputs Evidence of activities Other materials demonstrating implementation This criterion is important because the call is designed to showcase real-world examples of education innovation . 10. Community Impact Beyond Learning and Teaching Environments The project should ideally have an impact beyond the classroom or immediate learning environment. The organisers want to highlight projects that connect education with actual community needs. Applicants should therefore demonstrate how their work contributes to the wider community and addresses practical environmental, social or sustainability challenges. How Will Applications Be Evaluated? Each thematic area will be reviewed by a dedicated panel from the Education for Climate Secretariat, involving representatives from EACEA, DG EAC, and experts . Applications will first undergo an eligibility check. Eligible projects will then be evaluated using five main criteria: Ambition Multi-disciplinarity Participation Tangibility Community impact Each criterion is scored from 1 to 10 . Community impact receives additional weighting and can contribute up to 12 points . The overall evaluation can therefore reach a maximum of 52 points . This scoring structure means applicants should not focus exclusively on how innovative their idea sounds. They should also provide convincing evidence of participation, implementation, tangible outputs and real community impact . How to Strengthen Your Application Applicants can improve their submission by presenting their project as a clear story from problem to action to outcome . A strong application should answer questions such as the following: What sustainability or climate challenge were you addressing? Why was the project necessary? Who identified the problem? Who participated? What role did young people, educators or other stakeholders play? What activities were implemented? What educational methods were used? Which GreenComp competences were addressed? What changed because of the project? What evidence can demonstrate the results? How did the project benefit the wider community? Could another school, organisation or community adapt the approach? Where possible, applicants should support their claims with specific examples and tangible evidence. For example, instead of simply stating that a project engaged young people in sustainability , explain how many young people participated, what responsibilities they had, what activities they led and what measurable or observable outcomes resulted . What Do Selected Projects Receive? The call offers significant visibility and networking opportunities for successful projects. Presentation at Education for Climate Day 2026 Three projects will be selected from each thematic area. With three thematic areas, this means a total of nine project examples will be selected to present their work and discuss their outcomes at Education for Climate Day 2026. The event will take place on 22 October 2026 . Fully Funded Visit to Brussels Representatives of selected projects will receive a fully funded visit to Brussels to participate in Education for Climate Day 2026. This gives selected representatives an opportunity to: Present their project. Discuss their implementation experience. Share lessons learned. Participate in hybrid sessions. Meet other climate education practitioners. Exchange ideas with education stakeholders. Build connections across the European Education Area. Gain visibility for their work. The opportunity is therefore not simply about recognition. It provides a platform for knowledge exchange and collaboration among people and organisations working on climate education. Important Application Requirement: Verified User Status Applicants should note that they need to be a verified user to submit a project. The call advises applicants who need to update their user status to join an onboarding session . This requirement is important because completing the project submission may depend on having the appropriate verified-user status before the application is finalised. Applicants should therefore avoid waiting until the final day to resolve account or verification issues. Submission Requirements The Education for Climate Coalition states that applicants need to complete the required submission components, including the survey and blog . Only complete applications , including both required components, will be considered. Applicants should therefore ensure that they do not submit an incomplete application. Before submitting, it is advisable to check that: The project falls under one of the three themes. The project meets the geographic requirement. Concrete implementation has already taken place. The project is within the eligible five-year period where applicable. Relevant education actors have participated. GreenComp competences are addressed. The project covers at least one Education for Climate Innovation Area. Appropriate learning and teaching methods are explained. Tangible evidence is available. Community impact is clearly demonstrated. Both the survey and blog components are completed. User verification requirements have been met. Copyright, Privacy and Intellectual Property Requirements Applicants must also ensure that they have the appropriate rights to all media submitted as part of their project. This includes materials such as: Photographs Videos Music Documents Other copyrighted materials By submitting a project, applicants confirm that they either own the copyright to the media used or have the necessary licence or permission to use it. Applicants must also ensure that their submission does not violate privacy rights, copyright or other intellectual property rights belonging to another person or organisation. Plagiarism or copyright infringement can result in disqualification. This makes it essential for applicants to verify the origin and usage rights of every photograph, video, piece of music, graphic, document or other copyrighted material included in their submission. Key Dates for the Education for Climate 2026 Call The timeline is important for anyone planning to participate. Call opens: 18 June 2026 Application deadline: 6 September 2026 Selection notification: End of September 2026 Education for Climate Day 2026: 22 October 2026 Presentation of selected projects: 22 October 2026 in the hybrid event Deadline: 6 September 2026 Applicants should submit their complete applications by 6 September 2026 . Because the submission requires both the survey and blog, applicants should allow sufficient time to prepare their materials, verify their account status, and check that all supporting evidence meets the requirements. APPLY HERE Why This Opportunity Matters for Climate Education Climate change requires more than scientific knowledge. Communities also need the skills, values, participation mechanisms and educational approaches necessary to translate knowledge into action. This is where initiatives such as the Education for Climate Coalition s call become particularly relevant. The programme highlights education as a mechanism for helping people understand sustainability challenges while also giving learners and communities opportunities to participate in developing solutions. The three thematic areas also reflect different dimensions of climate education. Youth leadership focuses on agency and intergenerational collaboration . Citizenship education focuses on participation, institutional action and community engagement . GreenComp focuses on competence development and the ability to envision sustainable futures . Together, these areas provide a broad framework for demonstrating how education can contribute to the green transition. Who Should Consider Applying? The opportunity may be particularly relevant to organisations and individuals that have already implemented innovative sustainability education initiatives. You should consider submitting if you have a project that: Engages students or young people in climate action. Connects different generations around sustainability. Turns schools or institutions into living environments for sustainability. Brings families and communities into climate education. Uses education to promote green citizenship. Connects research with public education. Uses community knowledge to advance sustainability. Incorporates GreenComp competences. Helps learners imagine sustainable futures. Uses innovative teaching and learning methods. Produces tangible educational resources. Demonstrates meaningful community impact. Has already been implemented or is currently ongoing. Small projects should not automatically be discouraged from applying. The call explicitly welcomes initiatives of different sizes and from different types of education settings. Visit HERE for more information about the Innovative Green Education Action Projects 2026. Pro Tip for Applicants Do not describe only the idea behind your project — demonstrate the action and its impact. The evaluation criteria place significant emphasis on participation, tangibility and community impact. Therefore, applicants should make their submission evidence-based. Show: The challenge → the people involved → the action taken → the educational approach → the evidence → the results → the community impact → what others can learn or replicate. If photographs, videos, learning materials, reports, activity records or other documentation are available and can legally be shared, use them to demonstrate that the project has been implemented in practice. It is also important to explicitly connect the project to the selected thematic area, GreenComp competence and relevant Education for Climate Innovation Area rather than expecting evaluators to make those connections themselves. Final Thoughts The Education for Climate Coalition Call for Innovative Green Education Action Projects 2026 provides a platform for showcasing practical examples of how education can contribute to climate action and sustainability. The call is particularly valuable for projects that combine innovation with participation, education with action, and learning with community impact . Applicants can submit projects under three thematic areas: Youth Leadership and Intergenerational Dialogue for Climate Action; Citizenship Education and Institutional Action for Sustainability; and GreenComp: Envisioning Sustainable Futures in Teaching and Learning . Nine projects in total — three from each theme — will be selected to present their work at Education for Climate Day 2026 on 22 October . Representatives of selected projects will receive a fully funded visit to Brussels , providing an opportunity to showcase their work, exchange knowledge and connect with other climate education stakeholders across the European Education Area. However, applicants should pay close attention to the eligibility requirements. The project must be based in or across an eligible European Education Area country, have undergone concrete implementation, and satisfy the relevant thematic and evaluation criteria. Applicants must also complete all required components, including the survey and blog, and ensure that submitted media complies with copyright and privacy requirements. With the 6 September 2026 deadline approaching, eligible applicants with strong, already-implemented climate or sustainability education projects should begin preparing their submissions without delay. The strongest applications will clearly demonstrate not only what makes their project innovative, but also who participated, what was implemented, what evidence exists, and how the project created meaningful impact within and beyond the learning environment . title: Anheuser-Busch University & Early Career Opportunities 2026: Internships, Co-Ops and Full-Time Jobs for Students and Recent Graduates
summary: If you are a university student, recent graduate, or early-career professional looking for an opportunity to gain practical industry experience, develop professional skills, work alongside experienced professionals, and build a strong foundation for your career, Anheuser-Busch offers a range of University Early Career Opportunities designed to help emerging talent enter and grow within the company. Anheuser-Busch s early-career opportunities are designed around a learn-by-doing approach. Rather than limiting participants to classroom-style training, the company provides opportunities to gain hands-on exposure to real business functions and understand how different teams work together. The available opportunities include full-time positions, internships, and co-op programs across areas such as logistics, supply chain, procurement, technology, marketing, sales, finance, legal, sustainability, brewing, people, communications, corporate affairs, and other business functions. For students and graduates who want to develop practical experience with a major global beverage company, these opportunities can provide exposure to real business operations, professional mentorship, senior leadership, technical development, and potential long-term career growth. Opportunity Overview Anheuser-Busch describes its early-career opportunities as programs and positions created to help individuals at the beginning of their professional journeys develop through practical experience. The opportunities are particularly relevant to people who want to combine academic knowledge with real-world business experience. Depending on the position, applicants may be considered for: Full-time early-career positions Internship opportunities Co-op opportunities Talent programs Trainee opportunities Opportunities across technical and non-technical business functions The company s early-career approach is centered around giving new talent meaningful exposure to the organization and its operations. Rather than simply observing experienced employees, participants can gain experience working within business functions and learning how teams contribute to the company s broader objectives. What Is the Anheuser-Busch University Early Career Program? The University Early Career platform brings together opportunities for students, recent graduates, and early-career professionals. According to Anheuser-Busch, its early-career opportunities are designed to provide individuals with opportunities to learn through practical experience. This approach can be particularly valuable for individuals who have academic qualifications but are looking for opportunities to develop workplace experience. Participants can potentially learn how a large organization operates, understand professional expectations, collaborate with colleagues, develop technical and interpersonal skills, and gain insight into how different departments contribute to the company s operations. The programs are also designed to support professional development and help identify and develop future leaders. Types of Opportunities Available 1. Full-Time Early Career Opportunities Anheuser-Busch provides full-time opportunities for individuals who are ready to begin or continue their professional careers. These positions may be suitable for recent graduates and early-career professionals, although the exact eligibility requirements depend on the individual vacancy. Full-time employees can gain direct experience within their selected business function while becoming part of the company s workforce. Applicants should carefully review each vacancy because qualifications, experience requirements, location, and other conditions can differ from one position to another. Interested candidates can explore the company s full-time early-career opportunities through the official Anheuser-Busch careers platform. 2. Internship Opportunities Internships provide students and early-career candidates with opportunities to gain practical workplace experience. An internship can help bridge the gap between university education and professional employment by allowing participants to apply knowledge in a real business environment. Anheuser-Busch s internship opportunities can involve different areas of the business, depending on the positions available during each recruiting cycle. Interns may have opportunities to: Work on real business activities Learn from experienced professionals Develop technical and professional skills Understand organizational operations Collaborate with colleagues Gain exposure to business decision-making Develop their professional networks Explore potential career paths The company highlights the importance of hands-on experience as part of its early-career programs. 3. Co-Op Opportunities Anheuser-Busch also offers co-op opportunities as part of its early-career programs. Co-op experiences can be especially valuable for university students who want to gain professional experience before completing their education. Depending on the individual position, participants may be able to work within a specific business function and gain a deeper understanding of how their academic background connects with professional responsibilities. Because co-op requirements vary by position, applicants should review the eligibility criteria for each vacancy before applying. Key Benefits of Anheuser-Busch Early Career Opportunities One of the major attractions of these opportunities is the emphasis on professional development. Hands-On Business Experience Anheuser-Busch s programs are designed around learning by doing. Participants can gain exposure to actual business functions and workplace responsibilities instead of relying exclusively on theoretical learning. This type of experience can help students and graduates develop a better understanding of how organizations operate. Exposure to Multiple Business Functions Anheuser-Busch operates through a wide range of departments. Early-career participants can potentially gain exposure to areas including: Brewing Logistics Supply chain Procurement Marketing Sales Technology Communications Corporate affairs People and human resources Finance Legal Sustainability Brewery operations Craft operations This diversity means that individuals with different academic and professional interests may find opportunities relevant to their career goals. Mentorship and Senior Leadership Exposure Anheuser-Busch states that its early-career programs provide exposure to senior leadership through mentorship opportunities and facilitated events. This can be an important advantage for individuals who are still developing their professional identities. Interacting with experienced professionals can help participants understand workplace expectations, learn from established leaders, receive guidance, and build professional relationships. Professional Growth and Development The company emphasizes growth and development throughout its early-career opportunities. Participants can receive relevant training and gain exposure to business operations from the beginning of their experience. This development-oriented environment can help individuals build capabilities that may remain useful throughout their careers. Potential Leadership Development Anheuser-Busch describes its early-career programs as opportunities designed to support the development of future leaders and change makers. For ambitious students and graduates, this means the experience can potentially serve as an important first step toward long-term career advancement. Exposure to a Major Consumer Brand Anheuser-Busch operates a portfolio of well-known beverage brands and businesses. Its brand portfolio includes names such as: Michelob Ultra Budweiser Bud Light Stella Artois Cutwater Kona Working within such a large organization can expose early-career professionals to complex business operations, large-scale teams, supply chains, marketing strategies, consumer-facing activities, and corporate functions. Departments and Career Areas Anheuser-Busch s early-career opportunities span multiple professional areas. Technology Technology professionals can potentially work on systems, digital tools, data, technology operations, and other technology-related business needs. Technology opportunities may be relevant to students and graduates with backgrounds in computer science, information technology, data, engineering, or related fields, depending on the individual vacancy. Procurement Procurement is responsible for activities associated with acquiring goods and services required by an organization. Individuals interested in purchasing, sourcing, supplier management, contracts, and commercial operations may find procurement opportunities relevant to their career goals. Marketing Marketing opportunities can provide exposure to brand development, consumer engagement, communications, market analysis, campaigns, and other activities associated with promoting products and connecting with consumers. Sales Sales professionals contribute to customer relationships, commercial activities, market development, and revenue generation. Candidates interested in business development, customer management, commercial strategy, or related areas may find opportunities within this department. People The People function focuses on employees and organizational needs. Career opportunities in this area may be relevant to individuals interested in human resources, talent development, employee experience, organizational development, and related disciplines. Logistics Logistics is an important function for a company involved in manufacturing and distributing consumer products. Anheuser-Busch specifically highlights logistics as one of its career areas and features early-career experiences in this field. Craft The company also identifies craft as one of its career areas. This may appeal to individuals interested in specialized beverage and brewing operations, depending on the available position. Legal Legal opportunities can provide exposure to the legal and regulatory requirements associated with operating a major corporation. Candidates with relevant legal education or professional backgrounds should review individual job descriptions for specific requirements. Finance Finance professionals support important financial activities across an organization. Candidates with backgrounds in accounting, finance, economics, business, or related disciplines may find relevant positions depending on the available vacancies. Sustainability Sustainability is another career area identified by Anheuser-Busch. Individuals interested in environmental sustainability, responsible business practices, sustainability strategy, and related areas may want to monitor opportunities within this function. Brewery Brewery operations are central to Anheuser-Busch s business. Opportunities in this area may involve production, manufacturing, technical operations, quality, engineering, and other specialized functions, depending on the position. Corporate Affairs Corporate affairs can involve communications, stakeholder engagement, public affairs, and related activities. Candidates with backgrounds in communications, public relations, political science, business, or related disciplines may find relevant opportunities depending on specific vacancies. What Can Applicants Expect? Anheuser-Busch outlines several key elements of its early-career experience. Learning the Business New hires and program participants are given opportunities to learn about different functional areas of the company. The company emphasizes gaining an in-depth and hands-on understanding of how its teams operate. Participants can gain insight into how teams work together to support: Employees Customers Consumers Business operations Product development Production Distribution Anheuser-Busch describes this broader perspective as understanding the journey from seed to sip. Working Across Teams Large organizations depend on collaboration between multiple departments. Early-career participants can therefore gain insight into how different functions work together. For example, supply chain activities may interact with procurement, logistics, manufacturing, technology, finance, sales, and other departments. Understanding these connections can help young professionals develop a broader business perspective. Mentorship Mentorship is another important part of the company s early-career approach. Participants may have opportunities to interact with experienced professionals and senior leaders. A strong mentor relationship can help an early-career professional understand the industry, improve professional skills, and make more informed career decisions. Training and Development The company highlights robust training and relevant experiences as components of its early-career programs. This combination can help participants develop both technical capabilities and broader workplace skills. Application Process Anheuser-Busch outlines a structured recruiting and selection process for its early-career opportunities. Step 1: Find a Suitable Opportunity Applicants should begin by exploring the available full-time, internship, and co-op positions. Because requirements can differ between roles, candidates should identify positions that match their education, skills, experience, interests, and career objectives. Step 2: Complete the Online Application Candidates are expected to complete the application online. An updated resume should be submitted as part of the application process. Applicants should ensure that their resumes accurately reflect their education, work experience, skills, projects, achievements, and other relevant qualifications. Step 3: Complete an Assessment if Required Some positions require applicants to complete an assessment. The assessment is not necessarily required for every position. Certain roles may also require a secondary job-knowledge test designed to validate the technical skills needed to succeed in the position. Applicants should therefore read each vacancy carefully and prepare for any assessments associated with the role. Step 4: Resume and Assessment Review After the application, resume, and any required assessment have been reviewed, selected candidates may be invited to a first-round interview. Step 5: First-Round Interview The first-round interview provides an opportunity for Anheuser-Busch to learn more about the candidate. Candidates may be asked about their: Previous experiences Skills Achievements Career interests Motivation Professional goals Fit with the position Anheuser-Busch specifically recommends remembering the S.T.A.R. method. How to Use the S.T.A.R. Method The S.T.A.R. method can help candidates structure answers to behavioral interview questions. S.T.A.R. stands for: Situation: Explain the circumstances or context. Task: Describe what you were responsible for accomplishing. Action: Explain the specific actions you personally took. Result: Explain what happened as a result of your actions. For example, instead of simply stating that you are a good team player, you can describe a real situation where you worked with others to solve a problem, explain your responsibility, outline the actions you took, and conclude with the measurable or meaningful result. Candidates should prepare several S.T.A.R. stories before the interview. Useful examples can come from: University projects Internships Previous employment Volunteer activities Leadership positions Student organizations Community projects Entrepreneurship Academic challenges Group Business Case Assessment Selected full-time Talent Program candidates may participate in a group business case assessment. This stage is designed to evaluate qualities such as: Problem-solving Collaboration Teamwork Candidates should therefore prepare not only to demonstrate individual knowledge but also to show that they can work effectively with others. During a group assessment, applicants should aim to contribute meaningful ideas while also listening to other participants. Strong collaboration is not simply about speaking frequently. It involves communicating clearly, considering different viewpoints, helping the group move toward a solution, and maintaining a professional attitude. Final Interview Candidates who successfully progress through the earlier stages may meet with senior department leaders for a final interview. Some opportunities may involve panel interviews. This stage can be an important opportunity for candidates to demonstrate their understanding of the position, explain their career motivations, and show how their experience and skills could contribute to the organization. Candidates should again prepare their S.T.A.R. stories and be ready to discuss relevant experiences. Application Timeline and Deadline No specific closing date is provided in the information supplied for the Anheuser-Busch University Early Career Opportunities. Instead, Anheuser-Busch states that its early-career recruiting cycle takes place each fall for full-time, internship, and co-op opportunities beginning the following year. This means applicants should not wait until the last minute to begin monitoring vacancies. Because individual positions may have their own closing dates, candidates should always check the specific job posting for the most current deadline. Important: Deadline: No single overall deadline is stated. Individual vacancies may have separate application deadlines. Who Can Apply? The University Early Career Opportunities are primarily aimed at people at the beginning stages of their professional careers. Potential applicant groups include: University students Recent graduates Early-career professionals Candidates seeking internships Candidates seeking co-op opportunities Candidates seeking full-time early-career positions However, eligibility is position-specific. A candidate should never assume that meeting the general description of an early-career applicant automatically qualifies them for every position. Each vacancy may establish its own requirements concerning: Academic background Degree level Graduation date Professional experience Technical skills Location Work authorization Availability Specific certifications Other job-specific qualifications Applicants should carefully review the official requirements of the position they intend to apply for. Countries and Nationalities Eligible to Apply The information provided does not identify a universal nationality, race, or continental restriction for the overall University Early Career Opportunities. The opportunities presented on the Anheuser-Busch platform can be associated with specific positions and locations, meaning eligibility may differ between vacancies. Therefore, candidates from outside the United States should pay particular attention to the location and work-authorization requirements stated in the individual job advertisement. The safest approach is to review the eligibility requirements for each position before submitting an application. Is This Opportunity a Scholarship? No. The Anheuser-Busch University Early Career Opportunities are not a scholarship program . They are career opportunities consisting of internships, co-op positions, full-time early-career roles, and related talent programs. Is This Opportunity a Fellowship? No. The information provided describes the opportunities as early-career employment and experiential learning programs rather than an academic or research fellowship. Why Should Students and Graduates Consider Applying? For students and graduates, obtaining professional experience can be one of the most important steps toward building a competitive career profile. Anheuser-Busch s approach combines several elements that can be valuable to early-career candidates: Practical workplace experience Professional development Exposure to experienced professionals Mentorship opportunities Senior leadership exposure Training Cross-functional business exposure Teamwork experience Problem-solving opportunities Potential long-term career development The opportunity may therefore be particularly attractive to individuals who want more than a theoretical understanding of business. How to Prepare a Strong Application Applicants should approach the process strategically. Update Your Resume Make sure your resume is current and tailored to the position. Highlight: Relevant education Work experience Internships Projects Leadership experience Technical skills Communication skills Analytical skills Achievements Relevant certifications Avoid submitting a generic resume that does not demonstrate why you are suitable for the specific position. Research the Position Read the complete job description before applying. Identify: Required qualifications Preferred qualifications Technical requirements Responsibilities Location Experience requirements Application deadline Use this information to determine whether your background aligns with the opportunity. Prepare for Assessments If the position requires an assessment, prepare before beginning it. For technical positions, review the relevant technical concepts. For business-oriented positions, be prepared for problem-solving, reasoning, analytical, or situational questions. Prepare S.T.A.R. Stories Because Anheuser-Busch specifically recommends the S.T.A.R. method, candidates should prepare several examples from their previous experiences. Prepare stories that demonstrate: Leadership Teamwork Problem-solving Adaptability Communication Initiative Conflict resolution Time management Achievement Prepare for the Business Case Candidates applying to selected Talent Program positions should also prepare for group business case assessments. Practice analyzing business problems, identifying key issues, developing solutions, explaining your reasoning, and collaborating with others. Anheuser-Busch Talent Community Individuals who are not immediately ready to apply for a specific position can also join Anheuser-Busch s Talent Community. Joining the talent community allows interested candidates to stay connected with the company s career opportunities and receive information about potential opportunities. This can be useful for students and graduates who want to monitor future openings. Anheuser-Busch Careers Interested applicants should explore the company s official career resources to identify currently available positions. Applicants should rely on official job descriptions for the latest information regarding eligibility, location, requirements, deadlines, assessments, and application instructions. Application and opportunity information: Anheuser-Busch Careers Full-Time Early Career Opportunities: Explore Full-Time Early Career Opportunities Internship Co-Op Opportunities: Explore Internship Co-Op Opportunities Talent Community: Join the Anheuser-Busch Talent Community Frequently Asked Questions What are Anheuser-Busch University Early Career Opportunities? They are opportunities designed for students, recent graduates, and early-career professionals, including internships, co-ops, full-time positions, and talent programs. Are these opportunities paid? The supplied information does not provide compensation details for every opportunity. Compensation and benefits should therefore be checked in the individual job posting. Can recent graduates apply? title: Artists’ Contacts 2026: Apply for ifa International Arts and Cultural Exchange Funding for Projects in 2027
summary: The Institut für Auslandsbeziehungen (ifa) Artists’ Contacts programme 2026 is offering funding for international artistic and cultural exchange projects connecting Germany with countries of the Global South and countries in transition. The programme is designed to strengthen international collaboration, encourage knowledge exchange, support artistic mobility and create sustainable networks among artists and cultural practitioners across borders. Eligible applicants can seek support for a wide range of international visual arts and cultural activities, including working visits, research trips, exhibitions, artist-in-residence programmes, workshops, lectures, conferences, performances and other international exchange initiatives. The application deadline is 30 September 2026 , while supported projects are scheduled to take place between March and November 2027 . Applicants who are interested in using art and cultural exchange to promote diversity, democratic values, human dignity, social cohesion and environmental responsibility are particularly encouraged to consider the programme. About the ifa Artists’ Contacts Programme The Artists’ Contacts programme is an international funding initiative of the Institut für Auslandsbeziehungen (ifa) that supports artistic and cultural exchange between Germany and countries in the Global South and countries in transition. Rather than treating international mobility simply as an opportunity to travel, the programme places emphasis on meaningful cooperation, mutual learning and the creation of long-term relationships between cultural practitioners and institutions. The programme is particularly relevant to artists and cultural professionals who want to work across national and cultural boundaries, develop collaborative artistic projects, undertake research, participate in international exhibitions or residencies, and build sustainable professional networks. According to ifa, international artistic encounters can create spaces for dialogue, encourage different perspectives and contribute to mutual understanding. The programme therefore recognises art and culture as important tools for strengthening democratic values, social participation and responsible engagement with global challenges. What Is the Main Focus of Artists’ Contacts 2026? The central focus of the programme is intercultural exchange and networking in the visual arts . The funding supports projects that place collaboration and knowledge exchange at the heart of international artistic engagement. Applicants are therefore encouraged to develop projects that go beyond one-time travel or isolated activities and instead demonstrate the potential to establish lasting relationships and professional networks. The programme is especially interested in projects that contribute to: International artistic and cultural cooperation Knowledge exchange between cultural practitioners Sustainable international networks Diversity and inclusion Democratic values Human dignity Social cohesion Social participation Environmental sustainability Regional connections Long-term international partnerships Projects should demonstrate strong artistic quality while also reflecting the broader values promoted by ifa. Who Can Benefit From the Artists’ Contacts Funding? The programme is open to a broad range of professionals and organisations working in the arts and cultural sector. Potential beneficiaries include: Artists Curators Art mediators and art educators Art theorists Architects Designers Photographers Media artists Institutions working within the arts and cultural sector The programme is therefore not limited to one particular artistic discipline. Instead, it provides opportunities for a variety of visual arts and cultural practitioners to participate in international exchange and collaborative projects. Applicants should, however, ensure that their proposed project meets the programme s artistic, collaborative and international eligibility requirements. Which Countries Are Eligible? A major feature of the Artists’ Contacts programme is its focus on international cooperation between Germany and countries included on the Development Assistance Committee (DAC) list of developing and transition countries . Applications can be submitted from countries on the DAC list for projects taking place in Germany. Applications from Germany can also be submitted for projects taking place in eligible countries on the DAC list. This means that the programme provides a two-way framework for cultural exchange: Artists and cultural practitioners from eligible DAC countries can participate in projects in Germany. Artists and cultural practitioners based in Germany can undertake eligible projects in countries appearing on the DAC list. Applicants should consult the current official list of eligible countries before preparing their applications because eligibility depends on the country s inclusion on the relevant DAC list. Importantly, eligibility is not determined by race or ethnicity. The programme s geographic eligibility is based on the relevant DAC country classification and the applicant s location or residence in accordance with the programme rules. Key Eligibility Requirements Applicants should carefully review the programme requirements before submitting a proposal. The following conditions are particularly important. 1. The Project Must Demonstrate High Artistic Quality The planned project should have a strong artistic or cultural concept and demonstrate a high level of artistic quality. Applicants should clearly communicate what they intend to achieve, why the project is artistically significant and how the proposed international collaboration contributes to the development of the work or professional practice. 2. Projects Should Reflect ifa s Values In addition to artistic quality, ifa considers broader values when assessing applications. These include: Social relevance Diversity Environmental sustainability Regional connections International cooperation Social cohesion Democratic values Applicants should therefore avoid presenting international travel as an end in itself. A stronger application should explain the artistic, cultural and social value of the proposed exchange. 3. International Artistic Cooperation Is Required The project must involve artistic and content-based cooperation between Germany and eligible countries in transition or countries of the Global South listed under the DAC framework. The international dimension of the project is therefore fundamental to the programme. 4. Special Residence Requirements Apply to Projects in Germany For projects involving travel to Germany, the participating artistic and cultural workers from eligible developing or transition countries must come from a country on the DAC list and must currently live there. This requirement is important for applicants who may have nationality from an eligible country but currently reside elsewhere. 5. Additional Residence Requirement for Projects Outside Germany For projects taking place in an eligible DAC country, artistic and cultural workers who do not have German citizenship must have lived in Germany for at least five years. The programme does not fund trips to the applicant s country of origin under this arrangement. 6. An Institutional Invitation Is Generally Required Applicants normally need an invitation from a non-commercial cultural or exhibition organisation or an artist-in-residence establishment. The organisation should not be a profit-oriented gallery. An invitation is not required for research trips. The foreign institution issuing the invitation must also provide significant financial and/or other services as part of the project. 7. Commercial Projects Are Not Eligible The project must not be organised within a commercial context. For example, projects connected to commercial art fairs are not eligible. The sale of artworks also excludes a project from funding. This means applicants should clearly distinguish an artistic or cultural exchange project from a commercial activity. 8. Students Cannot Apply Projects by students are not eligible for Artists’ Contacts funding. ifa recommends that students seeking relevant international academic opportunities instead explore programmes offered by the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) . What Activities Can the Funding Support? Artists’ Contacts funding can support a wide range of artistic and cultural exchange activities. Eligible activities can include: Exhibitions Performances Artist-in-residence programmes Workshops Preparatory trips Research trips Working visits International symposia Conferences Lectures Other international exchange initiatives This broad range of activities makes the programme relevant to artists and cultural professionals at different stages of an international project. A research-oriented applicant, for example, may use the opportunity to undertake an international research trip, while another applicant may use the programme to participate in an exhibition, workshop, residency or international cultural event. What Costs Does the Programme Cover? The Artists’ Contacts programme provides support for travel and accommodation costs in accordance with the applicable Federal Travel Expenses Act. For artistic and cultural workers travelling from countries in transition and developing countries to participate in eligible projects, ifa can cover a number of expenses. These may include: Flight expenses Travel expenses Accommodation costs Visa costs Overseas health insurance Daily food allowance of EUR 28 per day The programme does not cover travel and care expenses for family members. For Germans and artistic and cultural workers who have lived in Germany for at least five years and are travelling to eligible countries outside Germany, support can include the following: Flight expenses Travel expenses Accommodation costs Visa costs Applicable daily food allowances Again, family members travel and care costs cannot be covered by the programme. Environmental Sustainability Is an Important Consideration The programme recognises that international cultural exchange often requires travel, which can have an environmental impact. For this reason, ifa encourages applicants to consider environmental sustainability from the earliest stages of project planning. Applicants are encouraged to: Consider the environmental impact of international travel. Prioritise sustainable forms of mobility where practical. Reduce the carbon footprint of their projects. Incorporate environmental considerations into project planning. Demonstrate responsible use of environmental resources. Environmental sustainability is also one of the aspects considered when assessing the overall quality and relevance of proposed projects. How to Apply for the Artists’ Contacts Programme The application process involves four main steps. Step 1: Request Access to the Online Application Applicants must first request access through the official Artists’ Contacts application system. Step 2: Open the Link Sent by Email After requesting access, applicants receive an email containing a link through which they can create their online application. Step 3: Complete the Application Applicants should complete all required sections of the application. The system allows applicants to save their work and return to it later, meaning the application does not necessarily have to be completed in a single session. Step 4: Submit the Online Application and Send the Signed Hard Copy After submitting the online application, applicants must print it, sign it and send the hard copy by post to: ifa – Institut für Auslandsbeziehungen Artists Contacts Charlottenplatz 17 D-70173 Stuttgart Germany Applicants should allow sufficient time for the physical application to reach the organisation because the postmark deadline applies. APPLY HERE Documents Required for the Application Applicants should prepare the required supporting documents before submitting their application. The official programme lists the following key documents: Invitation Letter Applicants generally need an invitation from the relevant foreign cultural or exhibition organisation, unless the application concerns a research trip. Description of the Host Institution Applicants should provide information describing the cultural or exhibition institution involved in the project. Curriculum Vitae CVs should be submitted for all applicants for whom funding is being requested. The CVs should help demonstrate the applicants artistic or professional backgrounds and their suitability for the proposed project. Visual Material Applicants should provide visual material relating to the proposed project and/or examples of previous artistic work. This is particularly important because the programme evaluates the artistic quality of applications. Airfare Quotations Applicants must provide three quotations for airfare based on current fares. Applicants should therefore obtain current and credible flight quotations when preparing the budget and supporting documentation. Sound and video works can be provided as links in the upload section of the application system. Application Deadline for Artists’ Contacts 2026 The official application deadline is 30 September 2026 . The funding is for projects taking place between March and November 2027 . Applicants should pay close attention to the deadline because ifa states that no additional applications for projects taking place in 2027 will be accepted after 30 September 2026. The date of the postmark applies, and applications sent after the deadline will not be considered. Important Deadline Information Application deadline: 30 September 2026 Eligible project period: March to November 2027 Notification of decision: February 2027 Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day because the process involves both an online submission and a signed hard-copy application sent by post. Visit HERE for more information about the Artists’ Contacts Programme 2026. What Happens After You Apply? Once applications have been submitted, they are assessed through the programme s annual selection process. An expert jury meets once a year to decide which projects will receive funding. Funding decisions and the amount awarded depend on the available IFA budget and the applications received. Applicants will receive written notification of acceptance or rejection in February 2027 . Applicants should also be aware of several important conditions surrounding the decision-making process: No reasons for funding or rejection decisions will be provided. Rejected applications cannot be resubmitted. There is no legal recourse against the decision. Additional materials submitted with an application will not be returned. Projects that begin before approval cannot receive retrospective funding. Expenses incurred before approval cannot be reimbursed retrospectively. These conditions make it particularly important for applicants to wait for formal approval before beginning activities for which they expect to receive funding. How Can Applicants Strengthen Their Proposals? Although funding decisions are made by an expert jury and no outcome can be guaranteed, applicants can improve the clarity and competitiveness of their proposals by presenting a well-developed project. A strong proposal should clearly explain: What the project is about – Describe the artistic or cultural concept in clear terms. Why international cooperation is necessary – Explain why collaboration across Germany and the partner country adds value. Who is involved—Introduce the artists, cultural practitioners and host institutions. What the project will achieve – Define the expected artistic and cultural outcomes. How knowledge will be exchanged – Explain how participants will learn from one another. How the project can create lasting relationships—Demonstrate potential for continued cooperation after the funded activity. How the project reflects IFA s values—Address diversity, social relevance, environmental sustainability and regional connections where appropriate. How the budget will be used – Ensure requested travel-related costs are clearly justified. Why the proposed activities are appropriate – Link each activity to the project s objectives. How environmental impacts will be considered – Explain efforts to make international mobility as sustainable as reasonably possible. Applicants should also ensure that all required supporting documents are complete and consistent with the project proposal. Why Artists and Cultural Practitioners Should Consider This Opportunity International collaboration can be expensive, particularly when it involves air travel, accommodation, visas and other international mobility costs. The Artists’ Contacts programme can reduce some of these financial barriers and make international artistic cooperation more accessible. The opportunity can be particularly valuable for professionals seeking to: Expand their international networks. Collaborate with artists and cultural organisations across borders. Develop new artistic projects. Participate in exhibitions or performances. Undertake international research. Join artist-in-residence programmes. Organise workshops and knowledge-sharing activities. Participate in international conferences, symposia and lectures. Establish long-term institutional partnerships. Explore new cultural perspectives. Connect artistic practice with social and environmental issues. Beyond the immediate financial assistance, the programme s emphasis on sustainable international networks means that applicants can frame their projects around longer-term professional and cultural relationships rather than short-term travel alone. Important Restrictions Applicants Should Know Before applying, prospective applicants should carefully consider the programme s restrictions. The following are particularly important: Commercial projects are not eligible. Art fairs and similar commercial activities do not qualify. Selling artworks excludes funding. Student projects are not eligible. Trips to an applicant s country of origin are not permitted in the relevant projects involving non-German citizens residing in Germany. Projects that have already started cannot receive retrospective funding. Expenses incurred before approval cannot be reimbursed retrospectively. Family members travel and care expenses are not covered. Applicants cannot resubmit rejected applications. Funding is subject to the available budget. Approved funding represents the maximum amount payable subject to the relevant rules and receipts. Applicants should comply with the applicable German Federal Budget Code requirements when spending programme funds. A Global Opportunity for Visual Arts and Cultural Exchange The Artists’ Contacts programme stands out because it combines artistic mobility with broader objectives around international cooperation and intercultural understanding. For artists and cultural practitioners in eligible countries, the programme can provide an avenue to establish professional connections in Germany. For Germany-based practitioners, it can facilitate collaborations and exchange projects in eligible countries of the Global South and countries in transition. The programme s approach reflects a wider understanding of the role of culture in international relations. Artistic exchange can provide opportunities for people from different backgrounds to meet, share ideas, challenge assumptions and develop new approaches to common challenges. The emphasis on democracy, diversity, human dignity, social cohesion and environmental responsibility also means that projects with wider cultural or social relevance may be particularly well aligned with the programme s objectives. Where to Apply Interested applicants should use the official ifa Artists’ Contacts application system and carefully review the programme s eligibility conditions and supporting documents before submitting their applications. The official application process requires applicants to request access, create their online application, complete and submit it electronically, and then print, sign and send the application by post to ifa in Stuttgart. Application deadline: 30 September 2026 Project period: March to November 2027 Conclusion The ifa Artists’ Contacts 2026 funding programme presents an important opportunity for artists, curators, art mediators, art theorists, architects, designers and cultural institutions seeking to develop meaningful international collaborations between Germany and eligible countries in the Global South and countries in transition. Through support for travel, accommodation, visas, insurance and daily allowances, the programme can help reduce some of the financial barriers associated with international artistic mobility. It also supports a wide range of activities, from exhibitions and performances to research trips, workshops, artist residencies, lectures, conferences and other forms of cultural exchange. However, applicants should pay close attention to the eligibility requirements. Projects must demonstrate high artistic quality, involve genuine international cooperation and generally have a non-commercial cultural context. Residence requirements also apply depending on whether the project takes place in Germany or an eligible DAC country, while student projects are specifically excluded. With the 30 September 2026 deadline approaching, eligible artists and cultural practitioners should begin preparing their project concept, invitation documentation, CVs, artistic materials, budget information and airfare quotations as early as possible. Ultimately, the Artists’ Contacts programme is more than a travel funding opportunity. Its central objective is to encourage sustained international cooperation, knowledge exchange and cultural dialogue. For applicants with strong artistic projects and a clear commitment to meaningful intercultural collaboration, it offers an opportunity to build connections that can extend well beyond the funded project period.
